findings.issue: Spec §5 step 5 says a child killed by a signal makes the wrapper exit 1 and log 'apt-lock: <cmd> was killed by <SIGNAL>'. No test covers it. No SPEC item names a test for it, so this is not a SPEC violation.
findings.evidence: Mutant replacing the signal branch in runCommand (tools/ci/apt-lock.js:163-164) with resolve(0) survived the whole apt-lock suite. A manual run (`-- sh -c 'kill -TERM $$'`) does exit 1 with the log line, so the behaviour is correct today.
findings.fix: In 'runs the command at once when no apt lock is held', add a case `node -e "process.kill(process.pid,'SIGTERM')"`, and assert code 1 plus stdout containing 'was killed by SIGTERM'.

findings.issue: Spec §5 lists 'a positional before --' as a usage error. The stray-positional check (tools/ci/apt-lock.js:190-191) has no test because SPEC-09's case list leaves it out.
findings.evidence: Mutant `if (false) throw` at apt-lock.js:191 survived. A manual run (`--wait-seconds 1 x -- true`) exits 2 with 'apt-lock: usage: unexpected argument "x"'.

findings.issue: The last sleep is clamped to the time left (Math.min at apt-lock.js:138), so a final check happens exactly at the limit. Every test uses a wait that is a whole multiple of the poll (150/2, 1/0.2, 10/0.2), so removing the clamp is never noticed.
findings.fix: Add a fake-clock case with waitSeconds 5 and pollSeconds 2. Expect the clock to end at exactly 5000 and 4 checks (t = 0, 2, 4, 5).

findings.issue: Both devParts examples have majors below 0x1000, so the `(dev >> 32n) & ~0xfffn` term is never exercised. The examples are the ones the spec gives.
findings.evidence: Mutant replacing `~0xfffn` with `0n` in apt-lock.js:60 survived.
findings.fix: Optionally add a third example, e.g. makedev(0x1001, 0x100001) as a bigint, with its expected parts.

findings.issue: `if (line.includes('->')) continue;` is redundant. LOCK_LINE already rejects waiter lines, because the token after `->` shifts the pid column onto READ/WRITE. So the SPEC-06 waiter case passes either way.
findings.evidence: Mutant `if (false) continue;` survived. Behaviour is still correct, since the regex rejects '3: -> POSIX ADVISORY WRITE 999 …'.
findings.fix: Keep it as an explicit guard (it matches the spec wording), or drop it. No behaviour change either way.

summary: All SPEC items are implemented correctly. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Device encoding: /proc/locks prints MAJOR/MINOR(i_sb->s_dev) in hex. libuv builds st_dev on Linux with glibc makedev(stx_dev_major, stx_dev_minor), and devParts is the matching glibc decoder, so the match fires on the ext4 runner. Overlay or btrfs subvolume st_dev could differ, but neither applies on ubuntu-24.04 VM runners. Parsing handles POSIX/FLOCK/OFDLCK, '->' waiters, pid -1 -> null, hex major/minor with a decimal inode, and malformed lines (including '<none>'). ENOENT means free. Other stat errors are rethrown. comm lookup tolerates races (catch -> null). Timing: checks at 0, poll, ..., with a clamped final check at the limit. Exit codes: the child's code passes through (exit 7 verified). A signal gives 1 with a log line. A spawn error gives '::error::apt-lock: could not start …' and 1. Usage errors give 2. The child is spawned non-detached. retry.js spawns detached and kills the group, so SIGTERM and SIGKILL reach both the wrapper and npx, and no forwarding is needed. The ::error:: text matches §5 exactly. Both ci.yml steps are wired. Budget: 3x160+20 = 500 <= 780, 150+60 <= 240, and 13 and 20 are still asserted. The workflow.test.ts diff vs base is the one-line expectation edit plus the new AC#3 test only. tools/ci/retry.js is unchanged. The Linux real-flock test is meaningful: it builds no fake line and uses the default /proc/locks, so a devParts or matching bug would make the blocked run exit 0 and fail. Mutation testing ran on a scratch copy outside the repo, which was then deleted. 15 mutants: 10 were killed (the `<=` loop mutant hangs the fake-clock test, so it is caught, though not cleanly) and 5 survived. The survivors are listed as MINOR/NIT test gaps for behaviour that no SPEC item names a test for. The line count is 563 vs the 400 budget, a gate warn, not a fail. apt-lock.js has no unrequested abstractions.
